A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have solved the structure of a bacterial cereblon homolog and have shown that thalidomidelike compounds bind to the cereblon homologue in a manner that mimics the binding of a cellular ligand, uridine.

the binding pocket of cereblon, an E3 ligase that is responsible for the ubiquitination of proteins, is a highly conserved aromatic cage that is capable of recognizing and binding to a variety of ligands.
we have identified the binding site and the cellular ligand for cereblon, a protein that is essential for life and is the basis for several important anticancer drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thalidomidelike drugs are not specific cereblon ligands, but bind to a common binding pocket, and that this binding pocket is likely to be present in other proteins, including those of eukaryotes.
